name: St. Vincent Archabbey Basilica
history: Saint Vincent is the oldest Benedictine monastery in the United States and the largest in the Western Hemisphere. Its abbey church was designed by J. William Schickel, built from 1891 to 1905, and dedicated on 24 August 1905. Fifty years later to the day, in 1955, Pius XII declared it a minor basilica.
arch: A red-brick Romanesque Revival church with twin towers capped by white pyramidal roofs. A statue of the founding abbot, Boniface Wimmer, stands before it.
features: Monks from here founded many abbeys, including St. John's in Minnesota and St. Benedict's in Kansas.
The monks run Saint Vincent College and Seminary.

look.d: White caps on red-brick towers over the Pennsylvania hills.
Boniface Wimmer, the Bavarian monk who founded the archabbey, raises his hand in front.

fun: It was declared a basilica on the 50th anniversary of its dedication.
journal: The mother of American Benedictine houses. Red brick, white towers, Wimmer waving.

a: On the 50th anniversary of its dedication
